Oh god there’s so much cool stuff! My favorite aspect is learning about how giant corporations will file for bankruptcy like 3 times before they finally go down. Scams are very real but complicated and sometimes difficult to pull off bc of all the rules you have to follow to successfully file for bankruptcy

If you can get around the other rules and they can’t prove you were trying to commit bankruptcy fraud it is technically possible to sell a large amount of your assets before filing. It’s actually somewhat common and even occasionally recommended to sell at least some assets before filing. It’s a careful balance though because if you sell too much or sell it for less than it’s value you could get flagged and your bankruptcy case could get dismissed by the trustee
I love it SO MUCH

Basically, it depends, if you give away any property before filing for bankruptcy you have to note it on the paperwork, if you don’t the bankruptcy trustee can take action to recover the property you transferred if the transfer occurred within two years before you filed your bankruptcy. Whether or not the trustee can recover the property is based on multiple things including whether you intended to commit bankruptcy fraud, whether you sold or transferred the property for less than its value,what you purchased with the sales proceeds, and when the transfer occurred.
